title: How Tabs Chocolate engineered virality: volume posting, creator "franchises", and a product built to go viral
summary: Oliver Brocato explains how Tabs reached seven figures in year one with no paid ads. They designed a product that explains itself on camera, obsessed over launch details, then flooded TikTok, Reels and Shorts with content through creators on retainer running branded sub-accounts.

principles.text: Pick products that can go viral and sell themselves, with real barriers to entry, before spending on growth.
principles.quote: we had two pieces of criteria that we really wanted to kind of meet one being a product that can go viral and sell itself and two a product that has high barriers to entry and a level of proprietary nature around it

principles.text: Perfect the brand, design, unboxing and site before launch; agonize over every micro detail.
principles.quote: we wanted to ensure that before we launched we had everything perfect from the branding the design the unboxing experience the website we agonized over every single micro detail

principles.text: You can't predict which video goes viral, so win on volume at a quality baseline: buy the whole haystack.
principles.quote: it's not about picking the needle in the haystack it's about you know buying the whole haystack

principles.text: Put good creators on retainer and have them run branded sub-accounts, turning them into franchisees and locking in distribution.
principles.quote: we started to put good creators and influencers on retainer and we would have them post for us on a recurring basis they would post on their own page and then we would run subsidiary and secondary pages on tick tock

principles.text: When a video pops, double down fast; a follow-up reply to a comment with a call to action can outperform the original.
principles.quote: the secondary post responding to a comment on the original viral video will actually do better than the viral video itself despite getting like 1 10th 1 20th of the number of views

principles.text: Design the product so its concept is understood in seconds on camera; the clean-break chocolate square does this.
principles.quote: it explains the concept of what it is in a three second you know uh visual way without having to provide you know like paragraphs and essays of context
